findings.evidence: B-02 lists among its refusal causes "a member already present in persisted scope"; B-03 states "admitStaleRenegotiation calls it before it publishes a snapshot or takes the run-state lock, so an extension refusal is a pre-admission refusal"; B-09's scenario is "a completed attempt whose replacement pair is still on disk and whose recorded extension set is {2,3}" repeated "with {2,3}, then with {2}, {2,3,4}, {2,4}".
findings.expected: The contract must sequence extension-set resolution against replay detection, so that repeating a completed request reaches replayOutcome and yields replay-completed-no-op / replay-conflict rather than a resolver refusal.
findings.observed: The revision states the order and the scope view, and each part of the clear condition is now met. B-03 fixes the insertion point as eligibility, then attempt-already-pending, then completedReplacementFor (:709-728, unmoved), and only then extension resolution, still before the branch-tip reads, the snapshot and the lock. It then names the view per branch under one rule: a non-replay request resolves against state.scope.slices as loaded, a replay against state.scope.slices minus the identities the trailing COMPLETED event records in its extensions. Under that view every member the completed attempt added is absent, so B-09's {2,3} resolves and reaches the value comparison as replay-completed-no-op, and {2}, {2,3,4}, {2,4} resolve and fail set equality as replay-conflict; a different target still reaches the same branch because completedReplacementFor is keyed by pair fingerprints rather than the requested target. B-02 is restated to take a persisted-scope view argument and to never read RunState, so the already-in-scope check is scoped by whatever view B-03 supplies. B-09 names the distinguisher in shape and code rather than message text: the replayed:true AdmissionOutcome member carrying code replay-completed-no-op with the completed attemptId (:620-656), or code replay-conflict, and never an extension-* code; its observable result asserts that per case, and the test plan adds the malformed-replay case that does return extension-slice-unknown. B-07 pins completion-time revalidation to the plain locked view so the two call sites cannot be confused.
findings.clearCondition: The contract states the order of replay detection and extension resolution (or the scope view the resolver sees on a replay), such that each of B-09's declared cases is reachable and yields the replay code it claims, and B-02's already-in-scope refusal is scoped to non-replay requests; B-09's observable result names how the reached replay code is distinguished from the resolver refusal.

findings.evidence: The definition of done now reads "this slice's declared gates are the evidence: `typecheck` (`pnpm run typecheck`), `acceptance:behaviors` for every behavior id in this slice's manifest, and the `tests` gate (`pnpm run test`) every behavior row binds — the same three ids the manifest declares".
findings.expected: The gates a behavior declares and the bar the definition of done sets should be the same evidence.
findings.observed: The manifest was only partly changed, so the definition of done now asserts something its companion artifact does not carry. Five rows declare acceptance:behaviors (B-01, B-02, B-03, B-08, B-09); ten do not (B-04 ["typecheck","tests"], B-05 ["tests"], B-06 ["tests"], B-07 ["tests"], B-10 ["typecheck","tests"], P-01 ["tests"], P-02 ["typecheck","tests"], P-03 ["tests"], P-04 ["tests"], P-05 ["typecheck","tests"]). Several of those rows are the reformatted-only regions in the revision evidence (B-04 and B-05 changed whitespace, not gate ids). So "acceptance:behaviors for every behavior id in this slice's manifest" and "the same three ids the manifest declares" are both false as written, and B-05, B-06, B-07, P-01, P-03 still bind the full-suite tests gate as their sole evidence with no typecheck beside it. The mismatch this finding named is now recorded in the definition of done rather than removed from it.
findings.clearCondition: Either every behavior row in acceptance-manifest.json declares acceptance:behaviors alongside typecheck so the definition of done's "same three ids" sentence is true of the file, or the definition of done's last line is narrowed to name only the gate ids the rows actually carry (and the rows that carry tests alone gain typecheck).

findings.evidence: B-03 states of the non-replay branch "this is the only branch that refusal can arise in", and lists the replay-branch refusals as "unknown, `HITL`, outside `afk.json`, colliding, or blocked by something in neither the view nor the set".
findings.expected: An invariant B-03 declares about extension-already-in-scope should hold for every request that reaches the replay branch, since replay detection is keyed by the pair on disk rather than by the request.
findings.observed: completedReplacementFor is keyed by the replacement pair's fingerprints, so any request arriving while a completed attempt's pair is still on disk takes the replay branch — including one with a different target or a different set, which B-09 answers as replay-conflict. The replay view subtracts only the identities the trailing COMPLETED event added, so a member that was in persisted scope before that attempt is still in the view and does draw extension-already-in-scope on the replay branch. That contradicts B-03's "only branch" sentence and its replay-refusal list, and it is one case where B-09's blanket "a different identity set … is replay-conflict" does not hold. No declared scenario is unreachable — B-09's enumerated sets are all the completed attempt's own additions plus a fresh member — so this is a stated invariant that overreaches its own rule, not a blocked test.
findings.clearCondition: B-03 either narrows the sentence to what the view rule supports (extension-already-in-scope cannot arise for a member the completed attempt itself added) and adds already-in-scope to the replay branch's refusal list, or states that a replay-branch member already in the pre-attempt scope is refused rather than answered as a replay, with B-09's "a different identity set" claim scoped to match.

state changes on refusal"; Failure Matrix row "Eligibility, extension or
  snapshot refusal"). This slice inserts the resolver into the documented
  admission sequence (`src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:781-840`) at exactly one
  place, **after** replay detection, and states the order because B-09 depends on
  it: eligibility, then `attempt-already-pending`, then
  `completedReplacementFor` (`:709-728`, unmoved), and only then extension
  resolution — still before the branch-tip reads, the snapshot publication and the
  lock. Which scope view the resolver is handed follows from that position, and it
  is the same rule in both branches — *the persisted scope as it stood for this
  request's own admission*:
  - **Not a replay** (`completedReplacementFor` found nothing): the view is
    `state.scope.slices` as loaded. A refusal is the pre-admission refusal above,
    and `extension-already-in-scope` is the code for a member already recorded —
    this is the only branch that refusal can arise in.
  - **A replay** (the pair on disk is a completed attempt's replacement): the view
    is `state.scope.slices` **minus the identities that same trailing `COMPLETED`
    event records in its `extensions`** — the scope the completed attempt was
    admitted against, reconstructed from the lineage that recorded the additions
    rather than from a second stored copy (the B-10 argument). Every member the
    completed attempt itself added is therefore absent from the view and cannot
    draw `extension-already-in-scope`, so the resolved set reaches B-09's
    comparison and the request is answered as a replay. A replay whose selectors
    are malformed as *identities* — unknown, `HITL`, outside `afk.json`, colliding,
    or blocked by something in neither the view nor the set — still refuses with
    that member's code, because a request whose members do not resolve is not a
    repeat of anything.
  Planner decision, recorded here because it is a sequencing call inside this
  slice's contract and reversible before merge: the alternative — resolve first and
  teach `extension-already-in-scope` to defer to replay — was rejected because it
  would make one refusal code conditional on state the resolver deliberately does
  not read, and because the shipped sequence comment at `:781-800` already fixes
  replay as the step decided "before anything is published".

findings.evidence: B-01 refuses "a comma-separated part that is not digits-only (the parseSliceIdList rule at src/cli-options.ts:293-315)", while B-02 declares a refusal for "one selector matching one slice by number and another by issue id".
findings.expected: The accepted selector language for --extend-scope should be declared explicitly for GitHub-issue selectors, since B-02's identity-conflict refusal presumes a selector can resolve by issue id.
findings.observed: B-01 now declares the digits-only rule to be the whole accepted selector language and states that it already covers both selector kinds the PRD names: a canonical slice number with zero padding preserved as typed, and a bare GitHub-issue id, because issues.md parsing stores Slice.ghIssue with the '#' already stripped (cells[1].trim().replace("#", ""), src/issues-parser.ts:80). It records the spelling call that '#278' and every other non-digit form is refused by that same message rather than normalized, so the resolver never sees two spellings of one identity, and B-02's extension-identity-conflict text now says both spellings are bare numerics, which is what makes the number-vs-issue-id collision reachable. Both halves of the parser regression surface are bound in the artifacts the established inline harness uses: positive evidence is --extend-scope 03,278 returning ["03","278"] in order, and the rejected-and-boundary evidence is --extend-scope 12,x, the new --extend-scope 12,#278, --extend-scope 12,12, the duplicated flag and the missing value, all in src/cli-options.test.ts, which is in fileScope.
findings.clearCondition: B-01 or B-02 states the accepted spelling of a GitHub-issue selector under the digits-only rule (for example, that ghIssue values are bare numerics and therefore already covered), and the test plan names one newly accepted issue-id selector alongside the existing rejected-part case.

findings.evidence: B-08's observable result is that the test "asserts one changed:true transaction, the single reloaded document containing both halves, and an interleave at beforeLockAcquired that leaves neither half on disk", while the definition of done promises "a test proves no document carries only one side".
findings.expected: The declared observation should be able to produce evidence for the obligation it is attached to.
findings.observed: B-08 now takes the second option in the clear condition. It states there is no seam inside the transaction body to name and restates the obligation as the evidence the observation produces: exactly one run-state write on the completion path — one transactRunState call returning changed: true once, with no second transactRunState, no saveRunState and no other scope writer — and one published document carrying both the COMPLETED event and the whole set, with 'no document carries only one side' explicitly proven structurally rather than by observing an intermediate document. The beforeLockAcquired interleave is relabelled in both B-08 and the test plan as the adjacent fact it can witness, the writer count is declared as its own test-plan observation, and the definition-of-done line is rewritten to the same single-write / single-document bar.
findings.clearCondition: B-08 either names a seam inside the transaction body that can observe a partial publish, or restates the obligation and its definition-of-done line as the single-transaction / single-document evidence the observable result actually produces.
